basics.name: Tom A. Lamb
basics.label: PhD Student in Machine Learning, University of Oxford
basics.summary: My research focuses on AI safety, robustness, and reliable machine learning. This includes work on certifying LLM judges and the relative calibration of teacher–student models, calibrating semantic confidence scores, and developing adaptive inference-time steering methods, alongside contributions to hallucination detection and universal in-context approximation for recurrent models.

work.name: Apple Machine Learning Research
work.summary: Working with Sinead Williamson and Michael Kirchhof on post-training for budget-aware agents.
highlights: Internship culminated in the paper ‘Rewards for Budget-Aware Multi-Turn Agents That Adapt to Arbitrary Test-Time Constraints’.

work.name: DeepMind / Torr Vision Group, University of Oxford
work.summary: Designed a framework for faithful knowledge distillation. Derived LP-based bounds on teacher–student confidence disagreement enabling formal analysis. Developed methods yielding more calibrated student models; resulted in our paper Faithful Knowledge Distillation.

work.name: University of Durham
work.summary: Proved new identities relating polylogarithmic integrals to multiple zeta values with Prof. Herbert Gangl.
